import pandas as pd,numpy as np,itertools,json
from scipy.spatial.distance import pdist,squareform
c=pd.read_csv('counts.tsv',sep='\t',index_col=0);z=pd.read_csv('zones.csv',index_col=0)['zone']
def perm(X,g):
    D=squareform(pdist(X,'braycurtis'))**2;n=len(g);g=np.array(g)
    def F(g):
        sst=D[np.triu_indices(n,1)].sum()/n;ssw=0
        for k in set(g):
            i=np.where(g==k)[0];ssw+=D[np.ix_(i,i)][np.triu_indices(len(i),1)].sum()/len(i)
        a=len(set(g));return (sst-ssw)/(a-1)/(ssw/(n-a)),(sst-ssw)/sst
    return F(g)
core=c.groupby(c.index.str[:2]).sum();rel=core.div(core.sum(1),axis=0)
zc=z.groupby(z.index.str[:2]).first()
f,r=perm(rel.values,zc.values)
# exact perm
cnt=0;tot=0
for comb in itertools.combinations(range(6),3):
    g=np.array(['B']*6);g[list(comb)]='A';tot+=1;cnt+= perm(rel.values,g)[0]>=f-1e-12
print(f,r,cnt/tot)
r2=c.div(c.sum(1),axis=0);print(perm(r2.values,z.values))
json.dump({"status":"completed_with_assumptions","results":{"pseudo_f":f,"r_squared":r,"n":6},
"assumptions":["Aliquots a-c of a core are pseudoreplicates; core is the experimental unit, so counts were summed per core (300 specimens) and converted to relative abundances, n=6 cores (3 per zone).","Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA on core-level data; exact permutation over 20 core labelings gives p=%.3f (minimum attainable 0.1)."%(cnt/tot)],
"exclusions":[],"issues":["Treating 18 aliquots as independent would inflate n and give pseudo-replicated F (%.3f, R2 %.3f); not used."%perm(r2.values,z.values),"With only 6 cores the permutation test has low power."],
"summary":"Pooled aliquots per core, Bray-Curtis on relative abundances, one-way PERMANOVA by zone with n=6 cores."},open('answer.json','w'))
